criterion_rewrites._note: Structural corrections to criteria that false-fail for reasons unrelated to the answer. Applied by corpus.apply_criterion_rewrites() to the whole corpus so 30 identical fixes live in one reviewable place instead of 30 overlay overrides.
criterion_rewrites._why: The reporter UPPERCASES the project it resolved (task 813 returned METNET for a plan asserting eq MetNet), and for a LAB scope it returns project: null entirely (task 812: project null, reporter_context.lab_codes [KAM]). So `reporter_plan.project eq "Kamm"` and `eq "MetNet"` both false-fail regardless of whether the report was right.

route_policy._note: Writes, exports and open-ended analysis are Container-CC's job, so these families must assert the ROUTE, not an NS-internal parser mode. `parser_plan.mode == unsupported` resolves to None on any turn that never reaches NS, so it fails unconditionally no matter what the product did — 3 of the 15 seed-0 failures were exactly that, across 23 variants.
route_policy._policy: Settled by the operator 2026-07-28: bulk export is CC's job. Consistent with what the route_gate family already blesses (route.cc_write_investigation: 'writes are deliberately CC's, not an NS unsupported'; route.cc_open_ended_analysis) and with three variants a previous wave hand-converted to this exact shape.
route_policy._2026_07_29_also_assert: A route assertion ALONE cannot tell a working turn from a dead one. Task 957 in the 2026-07-29 run hit error_max_budget_usd, replied null, and scored GREEN because `route eq container_cc` was its only criterion. Applied per FIELD so the three hand-converted variants keep their own stricter last_reply regexes.
route_policy._2026_07_31_mapping: Extended from 2 families to 12 from the operator's route mapping (issue #35 step 2). Every turn in the active corpus was assigned a route by an agent working only from route_capabilities.json, with no sight of the existing criteria, the operator's earlier answers, or any tags; the operator then reviewed all 311. 298 of the 302 comparable turns matched their round-2 family answers.
route_policy._2026_07_31_drop_is_conditional: `drop_field` is no longer blanket. corpus.guarantees_ns() keeps parser_plan.mode wherever the rule pins nextseek_query, because there NS definitely runs and the field is real and observable. Applying the old blanket drop to these families would have stripped it from 256 variants — the corpus gaining a route assertion while losing a stronger one, which reads as a strengthening. See tests/test_route_policy_drop.py.
route_policy._2026_07_31_either: search_tree, refine_and_recall and pipeline_nfcore are asserted as an ALTERNATION because the operator answered EITHER for all three: the NS/CC boundary for follow-ups, lineage and pipeline build-vs-launch is genuinely unsettled. An alternation cannot guarantee NS, so parser_plan.mode is dropped for those three.
route_policy._2026_07_31_per_case: nessie_green and nessie_route are provenance groupings rather than intents (their members span several task families), so each carries its own route as an override instead of inheriting a family default.
route_policy._2026_08_03_inert_overrides: An override is appended only `if "route" not in present` (corpus.apply_route_policy), so an entry for a variant that writes its OWN route criterion never fires. green.global_count carried exactly that: this map claimed container_cc while the case asserted nextseek_query inline and backed it with a `50,88[0-9]` reply guard, a number only the NS REST global count produces. The inline criterion was right, so the dead override was DELETED rather than the case changed. green.refine_recall's entry was the same shape and the opposite call: there the router is right, so the case was rewritten to container_cc and the override kept, now agreeing with the inline criterion instead of contradicting it. tests/test_inline_route_assertions.py fails on any future override that contradicts an inline route.

family_floor._note: Minimum OUTCOME assertion per family, applied by corpus.merged() to the LAST TURN of every variant in a listed family. Of 381 merged variants, 108 assert plan shape only and 194 assert only plumbing (api_ok / neo4j_ok, which say a request COMPLETED, not that it returned anything) — 79% cannot detect a wrong answer. Hand-editing 300 variants is not viable, so the floor is applied structurally.
family_floor._rules: A floor criterion is added only when the last turn does not already assert that FIELD, so a deliberate bound (e.g. row_count lte 20000) is never overwritten and never contradicted. Families not listed here get no floor. Tag a variant `no_floor` to opt out entirely.
family_floor._2026_07_30_retirement: routing_graph lost its floor because it lost its only variant: routing.gbm_study_count was retired with the other 25 GBM cases (issue #35), leaving the family empty. A floor on a family with no members is dead config, and test_every_floored_family_exists_in_the_corpus enforces that. Reinstating the variant means reinstating its floor entry.
family_floor._2026_07_28_correction: The first version of this floor asserted VALUES rather than OBSERVABILITY, and that produced 10 of the 15 failures in the seed-0 run — false failures on answers that were correct. Measured over the merged corpus, the old spec put an unsatisfiable criterion on 163 variants (`count gte 1` where zero is ground truth, e.g. 14 GBM graph variants and zero_result_zebrafish), 59 (`graph_not_truncated` where the honest answer is 10,688 rows against a 5,000 cap) and 64 (`reporter_result.ok`, which only run_reporter_summary sets — the 24 SRA/GEO/PRIDE variants go through generate_report_outputs). A floor exists to catch a criterion that cannot SEE the answer, not to assert what the answer is. So: `api_outcome_observed` / `graph_outcome_observed` (the outcome was observed, zero included), `graph_truncation_disclosed` (a cap is fine, a HIDDEN cap is not) and `report_produced_output` (either of reporting's two result shapes). Per-case value expectations belong on the case, not in the floor.
family_floor._2026_08_03_engine_agnostic: The floor is keyed on v.family, and the family names are ENGINE-shaped — search_advanced means the REST advanced_search endpoint, graph_query means Cypher. The parser is free to answer the same question with either engine, so an engine-shaped floor is an assertion the corpus never meant to make. In the 2026-08-03 seed-6 run advanced.find_me_sequencing_files_assoc, advanced.find_me_nhp_samples_from_study_2 and advanced.find_me_d_seq_samples_in_proje each routed nextseek_query correctly and were answered correctly by the graph (1765 / 408 / 1858 rows), and each went red — on api_ok and api_outcome_observed, which are False on a graph turn by construction. So every engine-flexible family now floors on ONE field, `outcome_observed` (evaluate.py), the disjunction of graph_outcome_observed / api_outcome_observed / report_produced_output. api_ok and neo4j_ok are GONE from the floor for the same reason: api_ok is False on a graph-answered turn and neo4j_ok is False on a REST-answered one, so either is an engine mandate wearing a plumbing check's clothes. graph_query KEEPS graph_truncation_disclosed — it returns True for a non-graph turn by design, so it is inert rather than mandating, and a hidden cap is a real defect. reporting KEEPS report_produced_output: a report that produced no output is a real failure whatever engine ran. This WEAKENS the floor, so the guard that it did not weaken into vacuity is the deliverable: a turn that produced no outcome at all still fails (test_floor_ops.py), and the seed-6 Bedrock-outage turn graph.what_mice_are_in_the_impact_st is replayed to prove it on real evidence. The engine-specific booleans remain available so a case that genuinely must use one engine can still assert it BY HAND.
family_floor._2026_08_03b_the_floor_could_only_reach_: Correction to the note above: of the three seed-6 cases it names, the floor change fixed exactly ONE. advanced.find_me_nhp_samples_from_study_2 already had an overlay override asserting route / graph_not_truncated / last_reply, so BOTH of its red criteria came from the floor. The other two were base variants writing parser_plan.mode eq new_search, api_plan.endpoint contains advanced_search and api_ok true in their own text, and apply_family_floor skips a floor entry for a field the last turn already asserts — so a floor edit can never relax an inline criterion, and their api_ok was never the floor's to remove. They needed overlay OVERRIDES of their own, added in the search_advanced block above. Those keep route inline, add graph_not_truncated (inert on a REST turn, so it mandates no engine but still catches a hidden cap) and a last_reply regex demanding a real UID prefix or an honest negative, and keep entity_sampletype_codes on the D.SEQ case because it PASSED on the graph turn. No count is asserted on either: ground truth for 1765 and 1858 is unsettled (issue #33). The vacuity guards live in tests/test_floor_ops.py — an empty reply, a confident answer about the wrong entity, a silently capped graph result and a wrong route each still go red.
